'''Ray H. Baughman''' (January 14, 1943 – April 18, 2025) was an American chemist and nanotechnologist renowned for his pioneering work in artificial muscles and carbon nanotube-based materials. He held the Robert A. Welch Distinguished Chair in Chemistry and served as the Director of the Alan G. MacDiarmid NanoTech Institute at the [[University of Texas at Dallas]] (UT Dallas).<ref name="UTDProfile">{{cite web |title=Ray Baughman - UT Dallas Profiles |url=https://profiles.utdallas.edu/ray.baughman |publisher=University of Texas at Dallas |access-date=April 18, 2025}}</ref>

== Early life and education ==
Baughman earned his [[Bachelor of Science]] degree in physics from [[Carnegie Mellon University]] in 1964. He then pursued a Ph.D. in materials science at Harvard University, completing his doctorate in 1971.<ref name="UTDProfile"/>

== Career ==
After completing his education, Baughman spent over three decades in industry, primarily with Allied Chemical (later AlliedSignal and Honeywell). There, he held positions ranging from Staff Scientist to Corporate Fellow. In 2001, he transitioned to academia, joining UT Dallas where he led efforts in nanotechnology research and education.<ref name="UTDProfile"/>

== Research ==
Baughman's research focused on nanoscale materials and their applications in energy, sensing, and actuation. His major contributions include:
* Artificial muscles: He developed materials that mimic muscle behavior, with uses in robotics and biomedicine.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Haines |first1=C.S. |last2=Li |first2=N. |last3=Spinks |first3=G.M. |last4=Aliev |first4=A.E. |last5=Di |first5=J. |last6=Baughman |first6=R.H. |title=Artificial muscles from fishing line and sewing thread |journal=Science |volume=343 |issue=6173 |pages=868–872 |year=2014 |doi=10.1126/science.1246906}}</ref>
* Carbon nanotube yarns and sheets: His laboratory pioneered methods for spinning nanotubes into high-performance fibers.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Zhang |first1=M. |last2=Atkinson |first2=K.R. |last3=Baughman |first3=R.H. |title=Multifunctional carbon nanotube yarns by downsizing an ancient technology |journal=Science |volume=306 |issue=5700 |pages=1358–1361 |year=2004 |doi=10.1126/science.1104276}}</ref>
* Energy systems: He contributed to technologies for energy harvesting, storage, and conversion using nanostructured materials.

He held over 100 U.S. patents and authored more than 480 peer-reviewed publications.<ref name="UTDProfile"/>

== Death ==
Baughman died on April 18, 2025, at the age of 82.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.dignitymemorial.com/obituaries/dallas-tx/ray-baughman-12345802 |title=Ray Henry Baughman |website=Dignity Memorial |access-date=April 20, 2025}}</ref>

== Honors and awards ==
* Elected to the [[National Academy of Engineering]] (2008)<ref>{{cite web |title=NanoTech Institute Director Ray Baughman Elected to National Academy of Engineering |url=https://news.utdallas.edu/faculty-staff/nanotech-institute-director-ray-baughman-elected-to-national-academy-of-engineering/ |publisher=University of Texas at Dallas |date=February 8, 2008 |access-date=April 18, 2025}}</ref>
* Chemical Pioneer Award from the [[American Institute of Chemists]] (1995)<ref>{{cite web |title=Chemical Pioneer Award Winners |url=https://www.theaic.org/award_winners/chem_pioneer.html |publisher=American Institute of Chemists |access-date=April 18, 2025}}</ref>
* Named to [[Scientific American]] 50 (2006)<ref>{{cite web |title=Scientific American 50: SA 50 Winners and Contributors |url=https://www.scientificamerican.com/article/scientific-american-50-sa-2006-12/ |publisher=Scientific American |date=November 12, 2006 |access-date=April 18, 2025}}</ref>
* Listed in [[Time (magazine)|Time Magazine]]'s 50 Best Inventions (2011)<ref>{{cite web |title=Transparent Material Breakthrough: One of Time Magazine's Best Inventions of 2011 |url=https://www.wpafb.af.mil/News/Article-Display/Article/399690/transparent-material-breakthrough-one-of-time-magazines-best-inventions-of-2011/ |publisher=Air Force Office of Scientific Research |date=December 2, 2011 |access-date=April 18, 2025}}</ref>
* Fellow of the [[Royal Society of Chemistry]]<ref name="UTDProfile"/>
* Fellow of the [[American Physical Society]]<ref name="UTDProfile"/>
* Fellow of the [[National Academy of Inventors]]<ref>{{cite web |title=Ray Baughman - NAI |url=https://academyofinventors.org/fellow/ray-baughman/ |publisher=National Academy of Inventors |access-date=April 18, 2025}}</ref>
* Tech Titans Technology Inventors Award (2015)<ref>{{cite web |title=Professors Earn Top Honors as Titans of Tech |url=https://news.utdallas.edu/faculty-staff/professors-earn-top-honors-as-titans-of-tech/ |publisher=University of Texas at Dallas |date=August 28, 2015 |access-date=April 18, 2025}}</ref>

== Educational outreach ==
Baughman founded the NanoExplorers program at UT Dallas, which introduces high-school students to advanced research in nanoscience.<ref>{{cite web |title=NanoExplorers Program |url=https://nanotech.utdallas.edu/for-students/nanoexplorers/ |publisher=University of Texas at Dallas |access-date=April 18, 2025}}</ref>
